hook: A carpenter's workshop full of specialist tools: tap each one in the picture, then give it its article.
intro: A picture hunt instead of a deck: one busy carpenter's workshop with 32 things to find, every one a precise craft word that ordinary conversation rarely needs — der Hobel, die Schraubzwinge, das Senklot, der Klüpfel hanging on the pegboard. The prompt asks Wo ist der Zollstock? and you tap it in the picture. Each find shows its label, coloured by its gender, then leaves a small tick in that colour, so you can see what you have already found. Once you have passed a run, the hunt turns harder: the prompt hides the article (Wo ist ___ Zollstock?), and after the find you choose der, die or das yourself. A tap on bare wall costs nothing; a tap on the wrong object tells you what you hit and you keep looking, and after three misses the right one is shown. No object is asked twice in the same run.
tips[0].title: The last part of a compound decides
tips[0].text: Most tools here are compounds, and only the last part counts. Schraube + Zwinge: die Zwinge, so die Schraubzwinge. Hobel + Bank: die Bank, so die Hobelbank — even though der Hobel lies on top of it.
tips[0].check.why: The last part is die Waage, so the whole word is die Wasserwaage.
tips[1].title: Same first part, different article
tips[1].text: Säge, Hobel and Schraube all start compounds here, but the ending sets the gender each time: die Bandsäge but der Sägebock and das Sägeblatt; der Hobel but die Hobelbank. Never copy the article of the first word.
tips[1].check.why: The last part is der Stock, so it is der Schraubstock — the first part, die Schraube, does not count.
tips[2].title: Tools in -er are der, -eisen is das, -chen is das
tips[2].text: A device named after what it does with -er is masculine: der Akkuschrauber, der Hobel, der Klüpfel. Words built on das Eisen stay neuter: das Stemmeisen. Little things in -chen are always das: das Ölkännchen.
tips[2].check.why: Every noun in -chen is neuter, whatever the word it comes from (die Kanne → das Kännchen).
remember[0]: The last part of a compound sets the article: die Schraube + die Zwinge → die Schraubzwinge, but die Schraube + der Stock → der Schraubstock.
remember[1]: -chen always makes a noun das: die Kanne → das Ölkännchen.
remember[2]: Der Fuchsschwanz is the carpenter’s handsaw, not only a fox’s tail.
